title: How many fold lines does each shape in the first row have?
description: The first row of shapes in the table of Chapter one has a triangle, a square, a pentagon and so on up to a decagon, each with equal sides and equal angles. Folding them one by one gives their lines of symmetry, and the counts form a number pattern. The video also checks the square, which has more fold lines than the two corner to corner ones.
teaching_notes: One idea: a shape with all sides equal and all angles equal has as many lines of symmetry as it has sides. Watch for students who count only the corner to corner folds of a square and miss the two folds through the middles of the sides.

source: Figure it Out Q8 (section 9.2, second block)
video_script.why: The child counts the lines of symmetry of each regular polygon by folding, and sees that the count matches the number of sides.
video_script.substitution: Cut each shape from paper and fold it every way the halves match, then count the fold lines.
video_script.anchor: the first row of shapes in the table of Chapter 1: a triangle, a square, a pentagon, a hexagon, a heptagon, an octagon, a nonagon and a decagon, each with equal sides and equal angles
video_script.payoff_line: Each shape has as many lines of symmetry as it has sides

final_answer.spoken: three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine, ten, which are the counting numbers starting from three

never_show: a square shown with only 2 fold lines
a hexagon fold from corner to corner shown as the only kind of fold
maths_rules: a regular polygon with n sides has n lines of symmetry
triangle 3 sides, 3 lines: one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side
square 4 sides, 4 lines: 2 corner to corner and 2 from the middle of a side to the middle of the opposite side
pentagon 5 sides, 5 lines: one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side
hexagon 6 sides, 6 lines: 3 corner to corner and 3 side middle to side middle
the sequence for the triangle up to the decagon is 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, the counting numbers starting from 3
slip: a square has 4 lines, not 2; an odd sided shape has only corner to side folds
video_script.design: One idea: the number of fold lines equals the number of sides. Shapes appear one after the other in the order of the book's table. Fold lines are teal.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a row of shapes in Chapter one.
<bookmark mark='row'/>The row goes from a triangle on the left to a shape with ten sides on the right.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many fold lines does each shape have, and what pattern do the numbers make?

beats.on_screen: the row holds still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a triangle with equal sides and equal angles is marked with small tick marks; a paper copy folds along a dashed teal line and the halves cover each other

marks.reg: a triangle with equal sides and equal angles is marked with small tick marks
marks.line: a paper copy folds along a dashed teal line and the halves cover each other

narration: <bookmark mark='reg'/>A shape with all sides equal and all angles equal is called a regular polygon. Every shape in the row is one.
<bookmark mark='line'/>A fold line where both halves cover each other is called a line of symmetry.

beats.on_screen: Given: eight regular polygons, with 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10 sides

marks.given: the numbers of sides of the eight shapes are written under them

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, there are eight regular polygons, and they have from three up to ten sides.

beats.on_screen: To find: the lines of symmetry of each shape, and the pattern of the numbers

marks.find: the words lines of symmetry and pattern are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find the lines of symmetry of each shape, and then the pattern of the numbers.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, the triangle: 3 fold lines, one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side; the square: 4 fold lines, 2 corner to corner and 2 through the middles of opposite sides

marks.tri: the triangle shows three teal fold lines, one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side
marks.sq: the square shows two teal lines from corner to corner
marks.sq2: two more teal lines join the middles of opposite sides, so the square has four lines

narration: <bookmark mark='tri'/>Step one, fold the triangle from each corner to the middle of the opposite side. That gives three lines.
<bookmark mark='sq'/>Fold the square from corner to corner, and the halves match. There are two such lines.
<bookmark mark='sq2'/>Fold it up and down and then sideways, and the halves match again. The square has four lines.

beats.on_screen: Step 2, the pentagon: 5 fold lines, one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side; the hexagon: 6 fold lines, 3 corner to corner and 3 through the middles of opposite sides

marks.pent: the pentagon shows five teal fold lines, one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side
marks.hex: the hexagon shows three teal lines from corner to corner
marks.hex2: three more teal lines join the middles of opposite sides, so the hexagon has six lines

narration: <bookmark mark='pent'/>Step two, the pentagon has five lines, one from each corner to the middle of the opposite side.
<bookmark mark='hex'/>The hexagon has three lines from corner to corner.
<bookmark mark='hex2'/>It has three more lines through the middles of opposite sides. The hexagon has six lines.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, the rest of the row: the heptagon 7 lines, the octagon 8, the nonagon 9, the decagon 10; each shape has as many lines as sides

marks.rest: the heptagon, the octagon, the nonagon and the decagon each show their teal fold lines
marks.match: under each shape the number of lines is written beside its number of sides and the two numbers are equal

narration: <bookmark mark='rest'/>Step three, fold the heptagon, the octagon, the nonagon and the decagon the same way.
<bookmark mark='match'/>Each one has as many lines as it has sides. That is seven, eight, nine and ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 4, the pattern: the numbers of lines go up by one each time

marks.up: the numbers of lines are listed in a row with a plus one arrow between each pair
marks.name: the words the counting numbers starting from three are written under the row

narration: <bookmark mark='up'/>Step four, look at the numbers in a row. Each number is one more than the one before.
<bookmark mark='name'/>These are the counting numbers, starting from three.

beats.on_screen: Step 5, check: fold the square once more and count the lines again; the count of lines equals the count of sides for every shape

marks.check: the square folds up and down, sideways and along both corner to corner lines, and the four lines are counted
marks.all: a tick appears beside each shape where the lines equal the sides

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step five, put the answer back in the question. Fold the square again and count the lines, and there are four.
<bookmark mark='all'/>For every shape in the row, the lines equal the sides.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10: the counting numbers starting from 3

marks.nums: the numbers are ticked off one by one

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Each shape has as many lines of symmetry as it has sides.
<bookmark mark='nums'/>The numbers are the counting numbers from three.
They are three, four, five, six, seven, eight, nine and ten.
